This is a synthetic measure for the hypothetical reference project. It does not assert that the real foxBMS reaction is late; it asserts that the reference project's allocated interval and the waits the reused configuration applies are not reconciled.
record_verbatim.objective: Compute whether the reaction chain the pinned source implements can close inside the interval FB2-SYS-SYR-000003 allocates, and record the arithmetic. The oracle is the sum of the configured waits the source actually applies between the stages of opening, taken from the application configuration at the pinned commit, compared against the allocated interval and against the contactor-mechanical figure the parameter registry records. The measure is expected to fail, and recording that it fails - with the arithmetic shown - is the honest result rather than a defect in the measure.

oracle_detail.residual_risk: The whole computation rests on configured values that the reference project may change. It is therefore a finding about the current configuration, not a permanent verdict, and the measure is written so that re-running it after a change produces a different number rather than a different opinion.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: It does not prove the reaction would actually take the computed time: the computation is a lower bound from configured waits, not a worst case, and a real run could be faster or slower. It does not prove the reference project's contactor meets the mechanical figure, because no part of this corpus has measured a contactor. And it does not establish that the requirement is wrong; it establishes that the interval it allocates and the waits the source applies are not reconciled anywhere.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: no contactor was opened and no timing was observed. It is not source_grounded: the contactor-mechanical figure is a registry parameter, not a property of the source. It is not a synthetic assumption about behaviour: what is assumed is a number in a parameter table, and the measure names it.
oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is a sum of configured values. The waits are read from the source's own configuration headers at the pinned commit, so they are not assumptions about the reference project; the mechanical figure is a parameter, and the measure says so. The comparison is arithmetic, and the arithmetic is the same whether or not the item is ever built, which is what makes it an analytical oracle rather than a measurement.

preconditions: The application configuration's waits are the ones the pinned source applies.
The parameter registry's contactor-mechanical figure is the reference project's declared figure for the mechanical stage.
record_verbatim.regression_selection: Re-run on every change to the application's configured waits, to the task cycle time, to the contactor-mechanical parameter, or to the interval the requirement allocates. This measure is the corpus's early-warning indicator for a timing-budget contradiction between the requirement and the configuration.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
